evidence.quote: "Poor thing!" said the old poet, as he went to open the door.
evidence.paraphrase: The old poet reacts with compassion and opens the door to the cold child.

evidence.quote: And he bent his bow, took aim, and shot an arrow at the old poet, right into his heart.
evidence.paraphrase: The boy shoots an arrow into the old poet's heart to prove his bow still works.

evidence.quote: The poor poet lay on the earth and wept, for the arrow had really flown into his heart.
evidence.paraphrase: The poet weeps after the arrow strikes his heart.

evidence.quote: "How naughty a boy Cupid is! I will tell all children about him, that they may take care and not play with him, for he will only cause them sorrow and many a heartache."
evidence.paraphrase: The poet resolves to warn children about Cupid causing sorrow.

evidence.quote: When the university students come from the lectures, he runs beside them in a black coat, and with a book under his arm.
evidence.paraphrase: Cupid is described as disguising himself to continue striking people with arrows across ongoing situations.
